title: Mysterious 'Little Red Dots' in Space Might Be Baby Black Holes!
summary:
Imagine a star that's not really a star. It's a giant black hole wrapped in a thick blanket of gas, glowing super bright. That's what astronomers think they've found! They call it a "black-hole star." It's hiding inside one of the mysterious "little red dots" that the James Webb Space Telescope has been spotting in the early universe.

These little red dots are strange. They shine like crazy, but they don't look like normal black holes. Some scientists thought they might be cocoons of gas around growing black holes. Now, a team led by Rohan Naidu found one called MoM-BH*-1, and it's a record-breaker. It shines 100 billion times brighter than any known star! And it has a special feature called a "Balmer break"—a sudden drop in light—that is three to four times stronger than anything seen before. That's like a fingerprint telling us this is something brand new.

So what's going on? The team thinks there's a black hole about 100,000 times the mass of our Sun at the center, surrounded by a super dense gas cocoon. The black hole eats gas from inside the cocoon, and the energy makes the cocoon glow. It's kind of like how a regular star shines, but way more extreme.

How did such a huge black hole form so early? One idea is that a supermassive star—thousands of times bigger than the Sun—formed just 150 million years after the Big Bang. Then it exploded and collapsed into a black hole, leaving behind that glowing cocoon. Over time, the black hole would eat away the cocoon from the inside. Eventually, we might see a normal supermassive black hole like the ones in galaxies today.

This discovery is a big deal because it could explain where all the supermassive black holes in the universe came from. They might all be the leftovers of the very first giant stars!
why_it_matters: Learning how black holes formed helps explain how galaxies—including the one our Solar System lives in—came to be.

keywords.explanation: A nickname for a hidden black hole wrapped in a glowing gas cocoon.
A powerful space telescope that takes pictures of very old and far-away objects in the universe.
A thick covering of gas and dust that surrounds something, like a black hole in this article.
A sudden drop in a spectrum of light that scientists use like a fingerprint.
A giant black hole hundreds of thousands of times heavier than the Sun.
The beginning of our universe, when everything first began expanding.

questions.question: What might be hiding inside the mysterious 'little red dots'?
options: Flying saucers
Ordinary stars like the Sun
Baby black holes called black-hole stars
Planets made of gas
questions.correct_answer: Baby black holes called black-hole stars

questions.question: What is special about MoM-BH*-1?
options: It was found by a school class
It is smaller than our Sun
It shines 100 billion times brighter than any known star
It is the closest black hole to Earth
questions.correct_answer: It shines 100 billion times brighter than any known star

questions.question: What do astronomers think sits at the center of MoM-BH*-1?
options: A planet the size of Earth
A white dwarf star
A moon made of gas
A black hole about 100,000 times the mass of the Sun
questions.correct_answer: A black hole about 100,000 times the mass of the Sun

questions.question: According to one idea, what formed just 150 million years after the Big Bang?
options: A tiny rocky planet
A supermassive star thousands of times bigger than the Sun
A galaxy like the Milky Way
A cloud of cold water
questions.correct_answer: A supermassive star thousands of times bigger than the Sun

questions.question: What will happen over time if the idea is right?
options: The cocoon will freeze into a planet
The black hole will eat away the cocoon and look like a normal supermassive black hole
The black hole will disappear completely
The star will become the Sun
questions.correct_answer: The black hole will eat away the cocoon and look like a normal supermassive black hole

questions.question: Why is this discovery a big deal?
options: It shows little red dots are safe places
It could explain where supermassive black holes came from
It proves the Moon has life
It means the universe is shrinking
questions.correct_answer: It could explain where supermassive black holes came from

background_read: The James Webb Space Telescope is a large space telescope built by NASA and partners to see very old, faint light from the early universe.
The Big Bang is the name scientists give to the very beginning of the universe.
Black holes are places in space with gravity so strong that not even light can escape.
Article_Structure: WHO: Astronomers led by Rohan Naidu using the James Webb Space Telescope
WHAT: Studied a strange 'little red dot' and found a record-breaking object called MoM-BH*-1
WHERE: In the early universe, far away in space
WHY: To understand how the first black holes formed and grew into supermassive ones

perspectives.description: They are excited because MoM-BH*-1 shines brighter than any known star and has a Balmer break unlike anything seen before.
They want more examples before concluding that all little red dots are baby black holes.
They hope the James Webb Space Telescope will find many more black-hole stars to test the idea.
